title: Trespass to person and to land

content.overview: Trespass to person includes assault, battery, and false imprisonment — actionable per se without proof of actual loss. Trespass to land is unjustified direct interference with possession of land. Consent, lawful authority, and private defence are principal responses.

sections.heading: Trespass to person
sections.body: Battery: intentional application of force. Assault: reasonable apprehension of immediate battery. False imprisonment: total restraint of liberty without lawful justification. Each protects bodily integrity and liberty.

sections.heading: Trespass to land
sections.body: Direct entry or placing of objects on land in another's possession without justification. Possession, not ownership alone, grounds the action. Continuing trespass may support ongoing relief.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead facts of force, apprehension, restraint, or entry. For false imprisonment, scrutinise statutory arrest powers. Distinguish BNS offences that may arise on the same facts.
